newsitem.title: USA: Novopharm gets U.S. approval for generic herpes drug.
newsitem.headline: Novopharm gets U.S. approval for generic herpes drug.

text.p: Novopharm USA Inc. said Wednesday its generic equivalent for a widely used treatment for herpes simplex virus is available for sale.

The patent on acyclovir, branded as Zovirax, expired Tuesday and Glaxo Wellcome Plc no longer has exclusive rights to sell the prescription drug. Sales of Zovirax in the United States totalled $488 million in 1996.
The medication is used to treat herpes simplex virus, which causes both cold sores and genital herpes, and Varicella zoster virus, which causes chicken pox and shingles.
Novopharm is a subsidiary Novopharm Ltd, a privately held pharmaceutical company based in Scarborough, Ontario, Canada.

The Food and Drug Administration gave final approval to Novopharm to market the drug Tuesday. The FDA also said Novopharm's generic drug acyclovir is bioequivalent and therapeutically equivalent to Glaxo Wellcome's Zovirax.
Acyclovir speeds the healing process by stopping the virus from multiplying and damaging healthy cells. Acyclovir is a treatment and not a cure, Novopharm noted in a statement.
